descriptionChirho: The core meaning of דַּי: sufficiency, enough, what is adequate; appears in various prepositional and pronominal constructions (כְּדֵי, בְּדֵי, דַּיָּם, דַּיֶּךָ) but consistently rendered as sufficiency/enough across languages — eng: enough/sufficiency, spa: suficiente/baste, hin: पर्याप्त, arb: كِفَايَة/كَافِيًا, kor: 충분히/충분한, swa: kutosha/ya-kutosha.

Temporal-frequentative idiom מִדֵּי meaning 'as often as, whenever, each time'; cross-linguistic evidence shows distinct temporal/iterative vocabulary — eng: as-often-as/whenever, spa: cada-vez-que/siempre-que, hin: जब-भी, arb: كُلَّمَا (whenever), kor: 매번-때마다 (every time), swa: kila-wakati/kila-mara (every time).

Prepositional idiom כְּדֵי meaning 'according to, in proportion to, as much as'; distinguished by proportional/conformity vocabulary across languages — eng: according-to/as-much-as, spa: conforme-a, hin: अनुसार (according to)/समर्थ्य-अनुसार, arb: بِحَسَبِ/بِقَدْرِ (in proportion to), kor: 에-따라 (according to), swa: kadri-ya.

Comparative use of כְּדֵי meaning 'like, as, similar to'; rendered with comparative vocabulary distinct from both sufficiency and proportionality — eng: like, spa: como, hin: जैसे, arb: كَ-كَثْرَةِ (as the abundance of), kor: 같이 (like), swa: kama (like).
